text: The Integration Test Plan family is new, so this document is version 1 with no predecessor. No section, identifier, number or date of an earlier version is kept, because no earlier version exists.
why: The work package asks for the next version of each output, and the family has no source file in any version; a next version cannot be derived from a missing source.
read: Folder listing of 09 Testing and quality; recursive search for a file name containing Integration Test; Template and Rules R8.2 (the next version is the highest v<n> of the family plus 1, and there is none).
confirm: The document owner confirms that no Integration Test Plan was issued before this run.
impact: Version 1 is authored from the sources the work package names and cites no predecessor.

text: Every wave gate exits on every journey test case of the wave passing with no open severity 1 or 2 defect, with a severity 3 defect allowed only with an agreed fix date.
why: No source gives an integration pass rate; the SIT exit of the test strategy is the closest stated threshold and is the one the same document applies to a release.
read: Test strategy version 3 sections 3 and 7; Template and Rules R1 U7 (a date is never raised as a gap).
confirm: The QA lead confirms the exit wording before the first wave gate is read.
impact: A wave gate is judged on passing tests and open defects and on no invented percentage.

text: Each wave runs one integration test cycle that closes its gate before the first release date of the wave; no test window, cycle length or start date is asserted beyond that.
why: The sources define the gate and not its calendar, and a release date may not be raised as a gap or moved by a gate.
read: Test strategy version 3 section 3; Template and Rules R5.6 and R1 U7; split plan release dates per business epic.
confirm: The delivery lead confirms the cycle count per wave in the delivery plan.
impact: The plan can be scheduled without asserting a calendar the sources do not give.

text: The synthetic fixture set is deterministic from a seed and a business date, holds the eleven classes the harness story names, follows the fixtures the wave stories already name, and holds no production value and no personal data. Its volumes and identifiers stay configuration.
why: The harness story fixes the mechanism and the classes and leaves the values to configuration; the plan may state the mechanism only.
confirm: The QA lead sets the seed, the business date and the volumes at the wave entry check.
impact: Every wave suite starts from one repeatable set and every gap in it fails as a fixture fault.

text: The evidence of a gate is the harness report keyed by build and the journey report keyed by story and business date, both kept with the build they prove and past the gate that reads them; no retention period and no report schema is asserted.
why: The stories state the keys of the report and leave its format and its retention open; a plan may fix what the evidence proves without inventing its form.
confirm: The QA lead confirms the report schema and the retention with the document owner.
impact: A gate is readable after the wave and no retention rule is invented.

text: In SIT a service of a later wave is represented by the published fake of its contract, every stubbed hop is named in the journey report, and a stubbed hop is never counted as a real-owner pass.
why: The wave composition of SIT is not stated, and the C dependency rule already allows a consumer to be built and tested against a published contract and its fake.
read: Test strategy version 3 section 2; Template and Rules R5.4 (class C) and R5.7 rule 2; RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG section 12.8.
confirm: The integration lead confirms the stub policy for each wave gate.
impact: A wave can be gated before every later service exists, and the report shows which hops were real.

text: The non-functional evidence of a wave gate is the two RWB-ITG-NFR stories, the NFT-J rows the non-functional test plan version 3 assigns to the wave, and the NFR level test cases of the wave journey; every other non-functional identifier stays with the per-service and system tests.
why: Neither the specification nor the non-functional plan states a test level per identifier, and the wave assignment of the journey tests is already fixed by that plan.
read: Non Functional Specification v3; Non Functional Test Plan v3 section 9 and the wave table; RWB-ITG-TE009-ITG; RWB-ITG-TE010-ITG.
confirm: The solution architect confirms the split between integration and system evidence.
impact: The integration gate reads a stated set of non-functional tests and duplicates none.

text: A wave gate is signed by the QA lead with the integration lead, on the report of the harness and of the journey. Roles only; no person is named.
why: No source names a signatory; the two roles that own the harness and the contract pinning are the roles that can read the evidence.
read: Test strategy version 3 sections 3 and 5; RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG section 10; AGENTS.md rule 4.
confirm: The delivery lead confirms the signatories when the gate process is agreed.
impact: Every gate has one named pair of roles and no gate waits for an unnamed approver.

text: RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is read as the wave 1 increment of one harness that serves all four waves: each later wave pins its own contracts and generates one stub per service of that wave, and the wave 1 criteria stay as the story writes them.
why: The test strategy gives the harness all four waves and the story scopes its criteria to the wave 1 services; reading the story as an increment keeps both statements true.
read: Test strategy version 3 section 10; RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG sections 1, 7 and 12.8; split plan (W1J01 sits in RWB-ITG-W1).
confirm: The QA lead confirms the harness extension per wave.
impact: One harness and four contract pins, with no second harness story invented.

text: In wave 3 the instruction to the firm is proven against the published contract of S9 rwb-partner served by its fake; the real-owner instruction, result, fee and review are proven in the wave 4 journey RWB-ITG-W4J01-ITG.
why: The wave 3 journey names S9 and the wave map places S9 in wave 4, so the hop cannot be a real-owner hop in wave 3 without contradicting the wave map.
read: RWB-ITG-W3J01-ITG section 1; Ownership Map v1 sheet Services; Template and Rules R4 and R5.6; RWB-ITG-W4J01-ITG section 1.
confirm: The integration lead confirms the stub of S9 in the wave 3 run and the real-owner hop in wave 4.
impact: The wave 3 gate does not depend on a wave 4 build, and the real partner hop is still proven once.

text: The plan is issued in Draft status. No approval of this version is recorded in this run.
why: The realignment run continues without a human approval gate, and a missing approval is recorded rather than waited for.
read: AGENTS.md realignment overlay (D-RCV-60); Template and Rules R1 U8.
confirm: The document owner confirms the plan before it is used as a release gate.
impact: No gate of this plan is treated as signed; the plan is usable for test design and for the gate definition.

text: Every release date is copied unchanged from the plan and marked (tentative), and the business date of each journey is the one its story names: 2026-11-25 for wave 1, 2026-12-15 for wave 2, 2026-12-14 for wave 3 and 2027-04-30 for wave 4.
why: Dates are fixed for the run as unchanged and tentative, and a business date is test data that may not move a release date or be raised as a gap.
read: Template and Rules R1 U7 and DL48; split plan release dates; RWB-ITG-W1J02-ITG, W2J01, W3J01 and W4J01 test data rows.
confirm: The delivery lead re-confirms the dates in the release plan.
impact: Every date in the plan is traceable to a source and none is raised as a gap.

text: Every owner in this plan is a service code and short name of the Microservice Ownership Map v1, a platform epic of Template and Rules R5.1, or a role label of the source; a team type is written as a suggestion only.
why: The plan needs one owner per element and the map names no test owner, so the owner of a table, an operation, an event, a workflow or a job is read as the owner of the test that pins it.
read: Microservice Ownership Map v1, all sheets; Template and Rules R5.1 and R5.3; AGENTS.md rule 4 (no names of people).
confirm: The delivery lead confirms the platform epic codes used for the shared pieces.
impact: Every test and every element has one owner, written as a code or a role and never as a person.
